questions.question: In Colombia, what do people call the loud, blunt, direct way of talking of people from Santander?
hints: If you're not used to it, it feels like you're being told off.
It's the exact opposite of a soft, sing-song way of talking.
It sounds as if every word lands a punch.
questions.fun_fact: Many people from Santander explain that they're not angry at all: that's just how they talk.

questions.description: A natural spa where the mud mask covers you from head to toe.
questions.question: Look at the map: the highlighted department is home to El Totumo volcano, where people float in mud. Which one is it?
hints: It's on the Caribbean coast.
Mompox, the town by the Magdalena River, is in this department too.
Its capital is Cartagena, the walled city.
questions.fun_fact: It's almost impossible to sink in El Totumo's mud: it's so thick that you float like a cork.

questions.description: There's not much to see in the desert by day, but at night the show is free and has millions of lights.
questions.question: “I live in the Tatacoa Desert, in Huila. At night, people come to look at the stars with me.” What am I?
hints: My work starts when the sun goes down.
From me you can see planets, the Moon and shooting stars.
Inside, I have telescopes.
questions.fun_fact: La Tatacoa is one of the best places in Colombia for stargazing because there are few clouds and almost no city lights reach it.

questions.description: A sport for people in a big hurry with even bigger patience.
questions.question: Colombian Éider Arévalo became world champion in 2017 in the track and field event shown in the photo. Which one is it?
hints: The judges watch very closely how the athletes move their legs.
Its classic Olympic distances were 20 km and 50 km.
Both feet must never leave the ground at the same time.
questions.fun_fact: In race walking, the supporting leg must stay straight from the moment it touches the ground until it passes under the body.

questions.question: Bogotá's main square faces the Capitol and the Cathedral. Who is it named after?
hints: He is a hero of Independence.
He is called “the Liberator.”
A department on the Caribbean coast carries his surname.
questions.fun_fact: The Bolívar statue in the middle of the square dates from 1846 and is Bogotá's oldest public monument.

questions.description: A glass house where the tenants pay no rent and fly in through the door.
questions.question: I have colorful wings, and at the Quindío Botanical Garden I live with hundreds of others in a huge house. What am I?
hints: I love drinking nectar from flowers.
Before I could fly, I spent some time sitting still inside a chrysalis.
Before I had wings, I was a caterpillar.
questions.fun_fact: Seen from above, the butterfly house at the Quindío Botanical Garden in Calarcá is shaped like a butterfly.

questions.description: In the orchestra everyone follows the conductor, though some pretend they can't see him.
questions.question: I have four thick strings, I'm almost as tall as a person, I'm played standing up, and I have the lowest sound in the string orchestra. What am I?
hints: You'll also find me in lots of jazz bands.
I can be played with a bow or by plucking the strings.
My name starts with a word that means “twice.”
questions.fun_fact: In many Colombian estudiantinas, the double bass joins tiples, bandolas and guitars to add the low notes.

questions.description: A name that sounds like the herbal tea grandma makes you before bed.
questions.question: In the San Andrés and Providencia archipelago there is a place called Quitasueño. What is it?
hints: It lies far from the inhabited islands, north of Providencia.
Almost all of it is underwater.
Ships fear it because they can run aground there.
questions.fun_fact: In 2012, the International Court of Justice confirmed that Quitasueño belongs to Colombia, in its dispute with Nicaragua.

questions.description: To pick a landing spot on Mars, NASA had to look very, very far back in time.
questions.question: The Perseverance rover, which Colombian Diana Trujillo worked on, landed in Jezero Crater. Why did NASA choose it? Because long ago there was…
hints: NASA was looking for a place where tiny life might have existed long ago.
From orbit you can see a delta, like the one a river makes where it ends.
Still water sat there billions of years ago.
questions.fun_fact: Perseverance stores rock samples in sealed tubes so a future mission can bring them back to Earth.

questions.description: The rule that makes your dad check the calendar before taking the car out.
questions.question: In Bogotá and Medellín, depending on the day of the week, some cars can't be driven at the busiest hours. What is this rule called?
hints: It changes with the day of the week.
It depends on the numbers on the front and back of the car.
Its name joins the Spanish for “rush hour” with the Spanish for what shows a car's number.
questions.fun_fact: Bogotá started pico y placa in 1998, and many other Colombian cities later copied the idea.

questions.question: It's measured in points every night, and if it's too low, a telenovela can be taken off the air. What is it?
hints: It shows up in the entertainment news the next day.
Caracol and RCN fight over it every night.
It's how many people are tuned in to a TV show.
questions.fun_fact: “Yo soy Betty, la fea” reached some of the highest ratings in the history of Colombian television.
